peircean_analysis.firstness: Four artifacts: (1) PDF audit report — author=jmartinez (internal Nexus employee), template=Informe_interno_v3.dotx (Nexus internal), created 2026-04-10 02:14 (2 days post-dated), PNG digital signature. (2) SAP log — DOC ID gaps (thousands of missing transactions), all entries APPROVED/same user/same account 6210, no milliseconds, exported same day as report. (3) Dashboard screenshot — processed through Photoshop, ELA detects edits at financial totals, created 01:58 (16 minutes before PDF). (4) Email headers — X-Originating-IP Argentine, originated from mail.nexus-corp.com (internal server), grant-associates.com registered 13 days prior, wrong mail client (Outlook vs Gmail).
peircean_analysis.secondness: All four artifacts share the same creation window (2026-04-10 01:58–09:15) and all contain independent forgery markers that contradict their claimed provenance. An external audit report cannot be authored by an internal employee using an internal template sent from an internal mail server. The chronological sequence (screenshot→PDF→email) reveals a construction sequence.
peircean_analysis.thirdness: Coordinated four-artifact fabrication to conceal embezzlement (~291,750 USD via account 6210 consulting expenses). The forgery markers are clear and independent. Under the acquisition assurance gate (no verified acquisition metadata), this constitutes SUSPICION rather than MALICE — the underlying pattern is consistent with deliberate fraud but the acquisition chain does not meet the Daubert corroboration bar for MALICE.

refutation_protocol.refutation_outcome: H2 not fully refuted under acquisition constraints. SUSPICION is the correct bounded verdict.

devil_advocate: Without verified acquisition metadata, the PDF could theoretically be an examiner-modified version of an authentic document. The SAP log could be an incomplete export rather than a curated fabrication. These alternative explanations are weaker than H1 but cannot be categorically eliminated without verified provenance.
